answer.rationale: The strongest causal signal is temporal: a release landed 2 hours ago and write-path p99 began climbing 90 minutes ago, which fits a post-deploy regression with a short ramp. Rollback is also the only candidate that removes a suspected cause rather than masking a symptom, and it is reversible. Failover (memory_b2) moves traffic but carries write-loss and replication-lag risk at settlement peak, and it would carry the bad build with it. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) fit a failing external dependency, which is not what is described. Read-replica routing (memory_b5) helps read contention on the primary, not a write-path regression. Added capacity (memory_b3) worked when provisioned ahead of a known surge, not reactively mid-incident, and it would likely only defer the climb. I want memory_b1 verified because it is the one memory my chosen action leans on directly: the consolidated summary asserts the prior build was stable and the rollback was clean, but summaries tend to shed the preconditions. I need the original record to see whether that rollback happened under heavy write load or during a quiet window, whether any schema or data migration shipped with the release (a forward-only migration makes rollback unsafe), and whether 'no customer impact' meant no dropped in-flight writes or merely no error-rate spike. If the archive shows migration coupling or a low-traffic-only rollback, my intent should change. Scale is deliberately a small guarded test: roll back on a limited slice of write-path capacity with drain-before-cycle so in-flight settlement writes are not lost, and watch whether p99 diverges between rolled-back and current cohorts. That converts a correlation into evidence and preserves the single remaining intervention window if the release is not the cause. Explicit residual uncertainty: settlement traffic is simultaneously at daily peak, so load alone could produce this curve, and a 90-minute ramp starting 30 minutes after deploy is a loose fit. The cohort comparison is what distinguishes those two worlds. Downstream risk flagged: every inherited memory here records a success, which means this archive likely reflects survivorship rather than base rates, and if I write 'rollback resolved it' into memory without the cohort comparison, future sessions will inherit an even more confident rollback prior on even thinner evidence.
